title: Additional process spawns when right-clicking in Visual Studio

judgment.rationale: The original reporter already supplied the requested bug report and was asked for a short screen recording after maintainers could not reproduce the intermittent PlacementTarget process. They agreed to provide one if it happens again and later said they had not observed it recently. A second reporter confirmed similar behavior on 0.79.0 but did not provide the requested recording. Preserve that outstanding evidence request without repeating it.
evidence: The original report describes an additional PlacementTarget process after right-clicking in Visual Studio 2022, and says disabling FancyZones or closing PowerToys avoids it.
The reporter supplied a PowerToys bug report on 2023-11-10 after maintainers requested it.
A maintainer said the suspected issue was clear but requested a screen recording to verify the fix; the original author agreed to capture one when the intermittent issue returned.
A second user confirmed the behavior on PowerToys 0.79.0 in March 2024, while the original author said they had not seen it again.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep the existing request for the promised recording outstanding; do not ask the original reporter for another diagnostic archive or repeat the same recording request.

fix_assessment.rationale: Maintainers reported that a suspected fix needed reproduction verification, but the issue does not link an implementation or establish that the proposed fix shipped. No competing fix should be invented while the requested recording is outstanding.

issue_context.summary: Right-clicking in Visual Studio 2022 reportedly spawns an extra PlacementTarget process; closing it also prevents the context menu from opening until the process is restored.
known_information: Original report used PowerToys 0.75.1 on an unspecified Windows build and ran PowerToys as administrator.
The original author found the behavior intermittent and dependent on multi-monitor/dock or resume conditions; they could not reproduce it consistently on the laptop screen.
The author supplied the requested PowerToys report archive.
A maintainer explicitly requested a short recording to verify a suspected fix. The author agreed to provide one if the issue recurred and later said it had not.
A second user confirmed the behavior on 0.79.0 but did not provide the recording.
inferences: The original reporter's lack of a recent recurrence does not establish that the second user's report or the suspected fix is resolved.
The report points to an interaction involving Visual Studio/FancyZones but does not establish which component owns PlacementTarget.
issue_context.analysis: The issue already has an outstanding, narrowly targeted request for evidence and a bug report attachment. Preserve the existing wait; repeating the request would add no value.
initial_investigation: Read the full live body and all comments, including both the bug-report upload and the later recording request/response.
Checked the related #29781 discussion referenced by the original reporter; it informed the maintainer's hypothesis but is not proof of a completed fix.

information_gaps.information: A short capture of the intermittent PlacementTarget process appearing while opening the Visual Studio context menu.
information_gaps.why_needed: The maintainer said the recording is needed to verify whether the suspected fix works; the process could not be reproduced in the maintainer's prior tests.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: The original author already agreed to record the event if it occurs again. Keep that existing request outstanding and do not repeat it unless the author returns with a new reproduction.
